digest.definition: Planning is the study of how societies plan, design, manage and regulate change in built and natural environments, and of why and how they intervene and with what effects
distinctiveFeatures: Planning is the study of how societies plan, design, manage and regulate change in built and natural environments, and of why and how they intervene and with what effects
Its academic core is the rationale for planning and how it is practised, taking in land and property markets, design and place-making, ecology and geography
It is inter- and multi-disciplinary and holistic, drawing on the social sciences and on environmental and design disciplines
It is about positive action: creative proposals reached through analysis, public participation and cooperation among competing interests
It is vocational and often professionally accredited, though it need not be; the RTPI alone confers Chartered Town Planner status in the UK
Learning is place-based and real-world: fieldwork, site visits, live projects and practitioners in the curriculum
Theory and practice form one continuing cycle, and the planner works as broker, visionary and advocate
Planning is devolved across the four UK nations, which share values and knowledge through professional and academic networks

enterprise linked to the values of planning and place-based leadership; modules on development business, land markets and climate enterprise; real-world projects with local authorities and communities (D1, 1.43 to 1.47)

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: governance differences across nations and abroad
statements.paraphrase: Planning education reflects global, national and devolved systems of government, and courses should allow for how law, policy, governance and practice differ, to suit their focus, in an increasingly international setting.

forPractitioner.text: Courses should take account of how the UK nations and other countries differ in law, policy, governance and practice, as fits the course's focus, and reflect structures at global, national and devolved scales.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Town and Country Planning degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: critical understanding of the contexts of planning
statements.paraphrase: A planning degree should aim to build students' knowledge and critical grasp of the environmental, political, social, economic, legal and governance settings in which planning works, and of how its frameworks change at local, national and international scales.

forPractitioner.text: The course should set out to develop students' knowledge and critical understanding of the changing settings of planning, from law, policy and administration to ethics, culture and power, at every scale from local to international.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course should help you build knowledge and a critical understanding of the political, social, economic, legal, environmental and ethical settings that planning works in, from local to international.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Town and Country Planning degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: wider skills and reflective, reflexive practice
statements.paraphrase: Planning degrees offer research and scholarship alongside professional growth and will build wider skills, among them negotiation, leadership, teamwork, communication, independent research and critical reflection; they should stress students becoming reflective and reflexive practitioners who grasp and act on the ethical demands of planning.

forPractitioner.text: Courses will develop negotiation, leadership, teamwork, communication, independent research and critical reflection, and should give weight to students growing into reflective and reflexive practitioners alert to the ethics of planning.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course will help you build skills in negotiating, leading, working in teams, communicating, researching on your own and reflecting critically, and it should help you become a practitioner who questions your own part in planning and its ethics.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Town and Country Planning degree
Characteristics of a Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: scholarship with practice; survey and data analysis
statements.paraphrase: Courses should normally combine scholarship with putting knowledge and skills to practical use, and should consider varied data sources and methods of analysis, with technology used rigorously and ethically, since planning rests on survey and analysis before plans and decisions; core learning usually comes before specialism.

forPractitioner.text: Courses should combine scholarship with practical application, and should teach survey and data analysis from varied sources, using technology with sound method and ethics; core knowledge and skills normally come before a specialism.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Town and Country Planning degree
Characteristics of a Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: interpersonal skills, real places and fieldwork
statements.paraphrase: Whatever the mode, full or part-time, in person or at a distance, students should get chances to build the interpersonal skills for work across professions and should meet real places in their full complexity; fieldwork, visits to sites and experiential learning should always feature in planning education.

forPractitioner.text: However the course is delivered, it should give students chances to develop interpersonal skills for cross-professional teamwork and to encounter real places, and fieldwork, visits and experiential learning should always be included.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: an inclusive curriculum and belonging
statements.paraphrase: Because graduates will practise in diverse societies, a barrier-free, inclusive curriculum is called essential, one that links employability to the careers of diverse groups and builds a learning community; students will be challenged to consider how to strengthen belonging for underrepresented groups.

forPractitioner.text: The text calls an inclusive curriculum essential: remove barriers so underrepresented groups can take full part, link employability to diverse students' careers and build a learning community in which students will be challenged to think about belonging.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be asked to think about how places and professions can help people from underrepresented groups feel they belong, and to learn in a community that welcomes everyone.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: knowledge of particular groups at every scale
statements.paraphrase: Students apply an inclusion lens at several spatial scales, from a site to the wider community, and will need to use knowledge particular to certain groups, such as how to remove barriers that keep underrepresented people from green space.

forPractitioner.text: Students will need to consider inclusion at different scales and draw on knowledge about particular groups, for example the barriers that people on low incomes, with health conditions or from minority ethnic backgrounds face in reaching green space.

forBeneficiary.text: You will need to think about inclusion at every scale, from one site to a whole community, and use what is known about particular groups, such as what stops some people using green spaces.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: inclusive design for the full range of learner needs
statements.paraphrase: Courses should be designed inclusively for the whole range of learner needs, recognising that access differs between groups and people, and care should be taken over how environments, materials, assessment and support affect learners with protected characteristics, neurodivergent learners among them, and from different socio-economic backgrounds.

forPractitioner.text: Courses should be designed for the whole range of learner needs: accept that access looks different for different people, and check how environments, materials, assessment and support affect students with protected characteristics or from different socio-economic backgrounds.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: accessible environments, adjustments and resources
statements.paraphrase: Every learning environment and set of materials should be open to learners with mobility or learning needs or with lived experience of disadvantage; students should receive reasonable adjustments for assessed needs, following national and institutional guidance, and programmes should try to give all students the facilities and resources to learn on and off campus.

forPractitioner.text: Learning spaces and materials should be accessible to learners with mobility or learning needs or lived experience of disadvantage; students should receive reasonable adjustments for assessed needs, and the programme should seek to give everyone the resources to learn on and off campus.

forBeneficiary.text: If you have assessed needs, you should receive reasonable adjustments, and your learning spaces, materials and resources, on campus and off, should be open to you.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: accessible settings beyond the classroom
statements.paraphrase: Planning is taught in many settings, from campus rooms to site visits, field trips, placements, group and live projects and digital learning, and particular care should be taken that each is inclusive and fully accessible, physically, socially and financially.

forPractitioner.text: Particular care should be taken that site visits, field trips, placements, group and live projects and digital learning are inclusive and fully accessible, with physical, social and financial barriers all considered.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: flexible recruitment and a curriculum students see themselves in
statements.paraphrase: Recruitment, apprenticeship routes included, should be flexible enough for learners from non-standard backgrounds or underrepresented groups to thrive, and content should be designed so that everyone recognises themselves in it, learns from others' varied experiences and is helped to explore future careers.

forPractitioner.text: Recruitment should be flexible for learners from non-standard or underrepresented backgrounds, and course content should be designed so that every student can recognise themselves in it, learn from others' experience and explore their career options.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: sustainability and critical thinking on the SDGs
statements.paraphrase: Sustainability runs through the teaching and content of planning education, and those delivering planning degrees should engage with, and encourage critical thinking about, the UN SDGs, other frameworks and sustainability in general.

forPractitioner.text: Weave sustainability through the course: it should engage with the UN SDGs and other frameworks and encourage students to think critically about them and about sustainability in general.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: embedding the SDGs across modules
statements.paraphrase: Courses should consider how to build teaching and learning tied to the UN SDGs into modules, working towards the goals and related frameworks such as the joint ESD guidance, with live projects, placements, case studies and practical examples as means.

forPractitioner.text: Courses should consider how to embed SDG-linked teaching and learning across modules, drawing on the joint ESD guidance and using live projects, placements, case studies and practical examples.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Town and Country Planning degree

statements.appliesTo: students of joint or combined degrees
statements.about: joint and combined honours
statements.paraphrase: Students on joint or combined degrees will gain the core subject-specific and generic skills set out in the statement and add others from their second subject, and may explore where the disciplines meet.

forPractitioner.text: Joint and combined honours students will reach the core planning skills, specific and generic, and add skills from their other subject, with scope to work where the disciplines overlap.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study planning with another subject, you will gain the core planning skills, both those particular to planning and the wider ones, add skills from your other subject and can explore where the two meet.

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: progression in judgement, independence and theory with practice
statements.paraphrase: As they progress, students' understanding of places grows more complex and critical and takes more account of stakeholders; they will show a growing grasp of the subtlety needed for situated, evidenced judgements on spatial and non-spatial questions, increasing independence in fieldwork and projects and an understanding that planning theory and practice form one continuing cycle of inquiry, reflection and improvement.

forPractitioner.text: Plan progression so that students will show more complex and critical understanding of places and stakeholders, finer situated and evidence-based judgement on spatial and non-spatial matters, more independence in fieldwork and projects using primary or secondary data and a sense of theory and practice as one cycle.

forBeneficiary.text: As you move through your course, you will make more careful judgements about places, grounded in evidence and context, carry out fieldwork and projects more independently and come to see planning theory and practice as one cycle of asking, acting and reflecting.

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Town and Country Planning degree

statements.about: external reviewers in periodic review
statements.paraphrase: Externality is central to UK quality assurance: providers will bring in external reviewers during periodic review for an outside view on proposed changes and to make sure threshold standards are met and content suits the subject.

forPractitioner.text: In periodic review, the provider will use external reviewers to give an outside view on changes and to confirm that threshold standards are met and content suits the subject.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: teaching designed with practitioners
statements.paraphrase: To bring theory and practice together, teaching and learning strategies should be designed jointly by planning academics and practitioners, joining theoretical ideas to real-life processes in an inclusive pedagogy centred on the student, with sustainability underpinning every pedagogic choice.

forPractitioner.text: Teaching and learning strategies should be designed by academics and practitioners together, linking theory to real-life processes in an inclusive, student-centred way, with sustainability behind every choice.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: practitioner involvement in teaching
statements.paraphrase: Teaching spans curriculum design, content, assessment, moderation and reflection, and the process, above all the delivery of content, should draw professional practitioners in actively so that real-world problems are tackled.

forPractitioner.text: Teaching, especially the delivery of content, should actively involve professional practitioners so that real-world problems are addressed.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: varied pedagogies for diverse learners
statements.paraphrase: Learning is change in a person through new information, understanding, skills, attitudes and behaviour, so varied teaching approaches are called for, suited to different learning styles and to hybrid, analogue and digital modes.

forPractitioner.text: Use a variety of teaching approaches to suit different learning styles and hybrid, analogue and digital modes; the text's wording ('are to be used') is obliging but not one of the usual modals.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: learning with stakeholders
statements.paraphrase: Learning opportunities should involve students actively with a range of stakeholders and may take in co-creation with academics or practitioners, interdisciplinary work, workplaces, scenario projects, simulations, problem-solving and community participation, alone and in groups; such a mix, which widens understanding of social, attitudinal and physical barriers, should be encouraged.

forPractitioner.text: Learning should actively involve stakeholders, through co-creation, interdisciplinary work, workplaces, scenarios, simulations and community participation, individually and in groups, and that mix should be encouraged.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: research skills and communicating research
statements.paraphrase: Research skills matter throughout the course and in practice, since places and their contexts need understanding before any intervention; through a research or design project they lead, students show independence and may frame questions and design a method; they will present their research to academic or professional audiences in a professional manner.

forPractitioner.text: Give students a student-led research or design project in which they can frame questions and choose a method; they will communicate their research to academic or professional audiences with professional skills.

forBeneficiary.text: You will develop research skills, often through a research or design project you lead yourself, and you will present your findings to academic or professional audiences in a professional way.

statements.about: evidence of achievement and Annex D
statements.paraphrase: Most students will do considerably better than the minimum threshold; each provider decides what counts as evidence of achievement and should refer to Annex D of the qualifications frameworks, which describes the four honours classifications.

forPractitioner.text: Decide your own evidence of achievement, referring as you should to Annex D, which describes the four honours classifications; expect most students to exceed the threshold.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: the standards students are expected to reach
statements.paraphrase: Students are expected to reach these standards in a planning degree and should show that they understand them and can apply them as fits their work.

forPractitioner.text: Students should show that they understand the standards and can apply them as fits; these are the standards a planning degree expects them to reach.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to reach these standards in your degree, and you should be able to show you understand them and can put them to use where they apply.

statements.about: interlinked interventions and environments
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates understand how planning interventions connect with one another and how they act on built and natural environments.

forPractitioner.text: At the minimum, graduates grasp that planning interventions are interlinked and affect both built and natural environments.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will understand how planning interventions link together and how they affect built and natural environments.

statements.about: solving problems with planning tools and processes
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates can find and settle problems using the tools and processes of planning.

forPractitioner.text: At the minimum, graduates identify problems and resolve them with planning tools and processes.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to spot problems and resolve them with planning's tools and processes.

statements.about: planning theory and its link to practice
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates know the theories of planning and the case made for its role in society, and how best to link theory to practice.

forPractitioner.text: At the minimum, graduates know planning theory, why planning exists and how theory bears on practice.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will know the main theories of planning, why societies plan and how theory connects to what planners do.

statements.about: the contexts and actors of planning
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates know the legal, political, economic, social and institutional settings of planning, the relative power of those involved and how planners can act within them.

forPractitioner.text: At the minimum, graduates know the legal, political, economic, social and institutional contexts of planning, who holds power in them and how planners can work within them.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will know the legal, political, economic, social and institutional settings planning works in, who holds power there and how planners can act.

statements.about: policy and how it is made
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates know what policy is, how it frames action at different scales, how planning policy comes about and how far it can shape outcomes.

forPractitioner.text: At the minimum, graduates know how policy frames action across scales, how planning policy is made and what it can achieve.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will know how planning policy is made, how it guides action at different scales and how much difference it can make.

statements.about: sustainable, inclusive places; design and finance
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates understand planning's part in creating sustainable and inclusive places, what design and finance add to that and why the needs of different groups count.

forPractitioner.text: At the minimum, graduates understand how planning, with design and finance, makes sustainable and inclusive places for different groups.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will understand how planning, helped by design and finance, creates places that are sustainable and work for different groups of people.

statements.about: planning, communities and diverse groups
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates understand how planning relates to communities and affects people and places, and how to work well with varied groups.

forPractitioner.text: At the minimum, graduates understand planning's relationship with communities and its effects, and how to work with diverse groups.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will understand how planning affects people and places and how to work well with the many different groups in a community.

statements.about: planning, climate and biodiversity
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates know how planning can address the climate and biodiversity crises, for instance through infrastructure that helps reach climate goals.

forPractitioner.text: At the minimum, graduates know what planning can do about climate change and biodiversity loss, including through infrastructure.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will know how planning can help deal with climate change and the loss of nature, for example through the infrastructure it plans.

statements.about: technology and digital settings in planning
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates can use technology in planning and appreciate the digital settings in which planning now takes place.

forPractitioner.text: At the minimum, graduates use planning technology and understand the digital environments planning works in.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to use technology in planning and understand the digital settings planning now works in.

statements.about: values, ethics and the profession
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates understand why values and ethics matter to planning practice and the profession's part in upholding them.

forPractitioner.text: At the minimum, graduates understand the place of values and ethics in planning and the profession's role in keeping them.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will understand why values and ethics matter in planning and how the profession keeps to them.

statements.about: working across disciplines and professions
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates understand how planning relates to other professions and disciplines and why working well across their boundaries matters.

forPractitioner.text: At the minimum, graduates understand planning's ties to other fields and the value of effective work across disciplines.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will understand how planning connects with other professions and why working well with them matters.

statements.about: research, evidence and weighing alternatives
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates understand why research matters to good planning, use evidence from varied sources and judge alternative policies and arguments.

forPractitioner.text: At the minimum, graduates value research in planning, use evidence from a range of sources and evaluate competing policies and arguments.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will understand why research matters in planning, use evidence from many sources and weigh up different policies and arguments.

statements.about: communicating in written, graphic, numerical and digital forms
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates communicate well in writing, graphics, numbers and digital media.

forPractitioner.text: At the minimum, graduates communicate effectively in writing, visually, numerically and digitally.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to get your ideas across clearly in writing, drawings and graphics, numbers and digital media.

statements.about: going beyond the threshold across the core themes
statements.paraphrase: At the typical standard, graduates meet every threshold criterion and will also go further than the minimum in what they know and understand, in thinking and practical skills and in professional competence.

forPractitioner.text: Typical graduates will meet all threshold criteria and go further in knowledge, cognitive and practical skills and professional competence.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the standard most students reach, you will meet every minimum criterion and go further in what you know, how you think, your practical skills and your professional competence.

statements.about: some critical judgement, initiative, creativity and autonomy
statements.paraphrase: At the typical standard, graduates will also show some critical judgement, insight, initiative, creativity and independence in applying the criteria well and fittingly.

forPractitioner.text: Typical graduates will show some critical discernment, insight, initiative, creativity and autonomy in how they apply the criteria.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the standard most students reach, you will show some critical judgement, insight, initiative, creativity and independence in how you apply what you have learned.

statements.about: excellence across all criteria
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent standard, graduates, having met the threshold and typical standards, understand and apply every criterion and will have taken their knowledge, thinking, practical skills and professional competence further than the typical level, to an excellent degree.

forPractitioner.text: Excellent graduates will understand and apply all the criteria and develop knowledge, cognitive and practical skills and professional competence to an excellent level, beyond the typical.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the highest standard, you will understand and use every criterion and take your knowledge, thinking, practical skills and professional competence well beyond the usual level.

statements.about: excellent critical judgement, insight, creativity and autonomy
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent standard, graduates apply the criteria fluently and with sophistication and will show excellent critical judgement, insight, creativity and independence.

forPractitioner.text: Excellent graduates will apply the criteria fluently and with sophistication, and their critical discernment, insight, creativity and autonomy will be of a high order.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the highest standard, you will apply what you have learned fluently and with sophistication, showing outstanding critical judgement, insight, creativity and independence.

statements.about: in-depth specialist knowledge
statements.paraphrase: Integrated master's graduates will, beyond the typical bachelor's standard, show deep knowledge of at least one specialist field of planning activity and practice.

forPractitioner.text: Integrated master's graduates will show in-depth knowledge of at least one specialist field of planning activity and practice.

forBeneficiary.text: On an integrated master's, you will build deep knowledge of at least one specialist area of planning and its practice.

statements.about: professional working, roles, ethics and values
statements.paraphrase: Integrated master's graduates will show a good grasp of how professionals work and the roles and responsibilities they hold, along with professional ethics and values.

forPractitioner.text: Integrated master's graduates will understand well how planners work and the roles and responsibilities they hold, along with the ethics and values of the profession.

forBeneficiary.text: On an integrated master's, you will gain a good understanding of how planners work and the roles and responsibilities they carry, along with the ethics and values of the profession.

statements.about: professionalism in assignments and group work
statements.paraphrase: Integrated master's graduates will show a high level of professionalism in carrying out assignments and in group work.

forPractitioner.text: Integrated master's graduates will work with a high degree of professionalism on assignments and in groups.

forBeneficiary.text: On an integrated master's, you will handle assignments and group work with a high level of professionalism.

statements.about: data and independent research
statements.paraphrase: Integrated master's graduates will use data collection and analysis effectively and be able to carry out independent research in planning.

forPractitioner.text: Integrated master's graduates will collect and analyse data effectively and conduct independent research in planning studies.

forBeneficiary.text: On an integrated master's, you will collect and analyse data effectively and carry out your own research in planning.
